main_text.l: fus ad idem vomitum reuertendo, & sic omni-
bus diebus vitæ fuæ suis concupiscentijs animas
suas maculant ; Confessio igitur plus affert
damni, quam vtilitatis . RESPONSIO.
Ne ex aequiuocatione errorem inferatis ; quo-
niam non omnem Confessionem vtilem esse di-
cimus ; sed eam peculiarem tantum, quae fit
post veram poenitentiam, quae est contritio
animæ de peccato patrato tempore præterito, &
discessus ab illo tempore præsenti, & promptus
recessus tempore futuro . Post adimpletionem
autem horum trium Canonum, si rursus suc-
cumbit natura, qua variabilis, & fluxa,
non est mirum, nec desperemus, oportet, præsertim audientes illud : septuagies septies . Di-
lucidatione porro secunda septem recenset
methodos, quibus animæ curantur morbi,
analogia eleganter deducta ex curatione
corporis morborum.
Ijdem Iacobitæ in suo Rituali integrum
instituunt tractatum sub hoc titulo :
[illegible, ~20 letters] [illegible, ~25 letters] [illegible, ~20 letters]
Ordo vniuersalis de omnibus iis, qui Confes-
sionem emittunt, prout præceptum est ; ex quo
nos breuitati consulentes hæc pauca :

page.notes: The first word of the page, "fus", is a fragment of a word broken from the previous page and is kept as printed. The Syriac title and the short Syriac line are printed in Syriac, which I could not read reliably at this scan resolution, so they are marked illegible rather than guessed. "RESPONSIO." is set run-in at the end of the paragraph, not on its own line, and is kept inline. "fluxa," is followed by a dash-like mark in print, read as a comma. Long s is transcribed as plain s throughout.
